parties:
MA Hannan ------------------ Petitioner
vs
Bangladesh and others--------Respondent
full_judgment:
5. During the pendency of the said suit on 1-9-2016 the petitioner made a representation to the respondent No.6 with a pray& to allow him to pay “ লেজার ব্যালেন্স স্থিতি ১২,৩১,৭৮,৮৭৬.৮৫ টাকা অথবা অর্থ মামলায় দাবিকৃত ১৩,৩০,১৮,২৮৭.৭৪ টাকা থেকে অনুমোদনবিহীন সার্ভিস চার্জ ওভার ডিও সুদ ও ফাইন পেনাল্টি বাদ দিয়ে।” at one go(Annexure-B). In response thereof the Board of Directors of the respondent bank in its 1065th meeting dated 21-9-2016 took decision to waive Taka 323.97 lac plus interest to be accrued up to the date towards full and final settlement against payment of Taka 1400 lac out of which Taka 50 lac to be paid within a month and Taka 1350 lac would be adjusted used within 29-12-2016. If, however, the petitioner failed to adjust the liability within the stipulated period he would be liable to pay the entire outstanding dues with interest (Annexure-C). 

 7. On 21-12-2016, before expiry of the stipulated period the petitioner made a representation to the respondent No.6 intimating the fact that against full and final settlement of the loan liability through payment of Taka 1400 lac the petitioner already paid Taka 900 lac by executing a "Baina" deed for selling off his landed property bearing Industrial Plot Nos,20-21, situated at Tejgaon industrial Area, Dhaka with Bangladesh Textile Mills Association and thus, would require extension of time for another 6(six) months with a view to obtain required permission/ approval of the concerned Ministry in order to dispose of the said property with machineries situated thereon. Accordingly, he requested the said respondent to adjust the payment of Taka 900 lac and to allow him to pay the remaining balance of Taka 500 lac within an interest free period of 6(six) months(Annexure-E). His prayer was duly allowed by the respondent bank vide office letter dated 8-1-2017 (Annexure-F) extending time period for another 6(six) months i.e. up to 30-6-2017 with interest rate 13% p.a. The petitioner, however, failed to pay the balance outstanding of Taka 500 lac within 30-6-2017 for not being able to obtain permission from the Ministry concerned. Under the circumstances, he again made a prayer to the respondent bank on 27-6-2017, prior to expiry of the stipulated period, for extension of time for another 3(three) months (Annexure-G), but there was no response. 

 9. In the meantime, on 26-11.2017 the petitioner deposited Taka 250 lac (Taka Two crore fifty lac) on 26-11-2017 and another Taka 250 lac (Taka Two crore fifty lac) on 28-11-2017 against the loan account of the Firm vide 2 (two) pay orders bearing No. PO1564486 and PO 1564515 dated 26-11-2017 and 28-11-2017 respectively (Annexure-I, I-1 and I-2 respectively). Stating the cause of delay in depositing the balance amount of Taka 500 lac Taka (Five crore) within time the petitioner made a representation to the respondent bank on 30-11-2.017 and prayed for adjustment of the said balance amount with exemption of all other interest/charges which had accrued during the said period and also to redeem the mortgaged property, bank shares and the FDR account offered as lien and to issue a redemption certificate in his favour (Annexure-J). Without giving any response thereto but admitting payment of Taka 1400 lac (Taka Fourteen crore) by the petitioner the decree holder bank filed Artha Execution Case No.4.36 of 2018 before the executing Adalat for realisation of the decretal amount to the tune of Taka 4,38,47,614.23(Taka Four crore thirty eight lac forty seven thousand six hundred fourteen and twenty three paisa) only, The petitioner entered appearance in the said case. Meanwhile, the executing Adalat fixed 7-1.2019 for auction of the mortgaged property under section 33(1) of the Artha Kin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, Ain, 2003)(Annexure-K and K-1 respectively), During the pendency of the execution case in response to the petitioner's application for consideration the respondent bank vide its office letter dated 8-8-2018 (Annexure-L) informed him that the Executive Committee of the Board in its meeting dated 1-8-2018 had approved waiver of Taka 9.40 lac (Taka Nine lac fourty thousand) only plus interest to be accrued upto the date of settlement in addition to the earlier waiver as approved on 21-9-2016 after realisation of Taka 200 lac (Taka Two crore) within 31-8-2018. The Committee also approved withdrawal of cases and release/redemption of collateral securities after adjustment of the settlement fully (Annexure-L). In reply thereof the petitioner vide letter dated 16-8-2018 explained the whole circumstances leading upto present and urged the respondent bank to adjust the entire liability of Taka 500 lac as per the sanction /approval Letters dated 26-9-2016 and 8-1-2017(Annexure-C and F respectively) as fully paid or impose additional penal interest for the additional period of 5(five) months and 26(twenty six) days at the rate of 12% and thereby redeem the mortgaged property, bank shares along with the FDR account kepi as hen and also to issue a redemption certificate in his favour (Annexure-M). Having receipt no response thereof on 8-11-018 he made a representation before Bangladesh Bank i.e., respondent No.2 describing all the state of affairs and thereby urged it to take necessary steps under section ৪৯(১)(চ) of the Bank Companies Act, 1991(in short, the Act, 1991) against Premier Bank Limited, Head Office, Banani, Dhaka and the respondent No.6 in connection with the petitioner's loan account(s) lying with the said respondent and thereby direct the respondent bank to redeem /release his property mortgaged, bank shares and the FDR account kept as lien.; in addition, to withdraw the pending legal proceedings along with issuing him with a redemption and/or no objection certificate, but with no response. 

 11. At this juncture, Mr M. Sayed Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that in compliance of the sanction/approval advices dated 26-6-2016 and 8-1-2017 of the respondent No. 6(Annexures- C and F respectively) the petitioner has already paid Taka 1,400 lac towards full and final settlement of his loan accounts; yet, the respondent bank with malafide intention not only refrained from releasing the petitioner's mortgaged property as well as bank shares and the FDR account kept as lien, but also claimed an additional amount of Taka 200 lac from the petitioner vide the impugned Memo bearing reference No.Premier/KBBI Cr/2018/3275 dated 8-8-2018(Annexure-L). In this regard, referring to section 8h(1)0) of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 he goes to argue that Bangladesh Bank was established by the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972 (PO No.127 of 1972) as a regulatory and supervising authority of the banking companies and financial institutions in Bangladesh and is empowered to inquire into and take steps regarding any action and inaction of any banking companies and to protect the rights of the customers of the banking company by taking appropriate steps against the said bank. Accordingly, he submits that since the petitioner had paid Taka 1400 lac as per the settlement agreement which is more than the amount so claimed in Artha Rin Suit No.1288 of 2015, i.e. Taka 13,30,18,287.74 hence, demanding an additional amount of Taka 200 lac by the respondent No.6 bank as unpaid dues vide the impugned Memo dated 8-8-2018 (Annexure-L) is illegal and not tenable in the eye of law. As such, he submits that upon making the Rule absolute the respondent Nos.1-5 are required to be directed to exercise the power as contemplated in section 811(0)M of the Act, 1991 in connection with the petitioner's loan account(s) lying with the respondent No.6 bank. 

 12. Conversely, Mr Tushar kanti Das, the learned Advocate by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondent No.6 submits that the petitioner has failed to make re-payment of his outstanding dues within the settlement period as well as within the extension period. Consequently, as per the terms and conditions of the settlement agreement the petitioner now becomes liable to pay the entire outstanding dues. Further, he submits that the petitioner in no way can seek waiver of his outstanding dues as of right, for, it is the absolute discretion of the respondent bank to waive interest. Moreover, earlier considering his prayer on different occasions the Board of Directors of the bank concerned had waived interest to certain extent and also upon extending time gave accommodation to the petitioner to pay off his outstanding dues, but he failed to comply making full and final adjustment within time. In this regard, drawing attention to office letter dated 12-7-2017 (Annexure -VIII) he goes to submit that consequent to letter dated 29-12-2016 when the petitioner failed to make payment within 30-6- 2017 the respondent bank had cancelled the arrangement towards final settlement as per sanction letter and, as such, the petitioner was liable to pay the entire outstanding dues with interest. But considering his subsequent prayer, the respondent bank vide letter dated 8-8-2018 (Annexure-V) again had waived interest of Taka 9.40 lac with direction upon the petitioner to pay Taka 200 lac by 30-8-2018 with approval to redeem collateral securities and withdrawal of cases after adjustment. But without making such payment the petitioner has filed the instant writ petition in the form of mandamus seeking direction upon the respondent No.2 bank for exercising power under section ৪৯(১)(চ) of the Bank Companies Act, 1991. In this regard, he goes to argue that admittedly over the defaulted loan amount judgment and decree has been passed by the Adalat on 20-7-2017 under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and that pursuant thereto an execution case have been filed for realisation of the decretal amount, which is still pending. Accordingly, he submits that since Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, the Ain, 2003) is a special law and has overriding effect vide section 3 of the Ain as such, the petitioner has no legal right to seek enforcement of section ৪৯(১)(চ)of the Act, 1991 in order to seek redeem/release of the collateral security and withdrawal of legal proceedings pending under Ain,2003. 

 14. Admittedly, over the claim of Taka 13,30,18,287.74 as the petitioner as the borrower and his wife, being the guarantor. However, in the plaint the respondent bank has categorically admitted payment of Taka 1,44,00.000 by the petitioner against his loan account. it, however, appears from record that during the pendency of the Artha Rin Suit on 01.9.2016(Annexure-B) the petitioner made a representation to the respondent bank with a prayer to pay Taka 12,31,78,876.85 or upon excluding the service charge, DO interest and fine/penalty from the amount of Taka 13,30,18,28714 (as claimed in the Artha Rin Suit) to pay the balance amount at one go. In response to his prayer the Board of Directors of the respondent bank in its 1065th meeting held on 21-9-2016 approved waiver of Taka 323.97 lac plus interest to be accrued up to the date of full and final settlement of the outstanding liability of Taka 1,723.97 lac as on 7-9-2016 against payment of Taka 1400 lac within 3(three) months from the date of approval.  However, Taka 50 lac to be paid within a month and the balance of Taka 1350 lac to be paid within 29-12-2016. In default, settlement arrangement would be cancelled and the petitioner would be liable to pay the entire outstanding dues with interest (Annexure-C). Accepting the said offer the petitioner duly paid Taka 50 lac on 29-9- 2016(Annexure-D) and Taka 850 lac on 20-12 2016 (Annexure-D-1) within the stipulated period i.e., within 29-12-2016. But failed to pay the balance Taka 500 lac within the said period. Drawing attention to the fact that “এখানে উল্লেখ্য যে, আমার নিজ নামীও তেজগাও শিল্প অঞ্চলের শিল্প প্লট নং ২০-২১ বাংলাদেশ টেক্সটাইল এসোসিয়েশনের নিকট বিক্রি করে রেজিস্ট্রি বায়না বাবদ উপরোক্ত টাকা পরিশোধ করিয়াছি। ৬ (ছয়) মাসের মধ্যে উক্ত এসোসিয়েশন মন্ত্রণালয় থেকে বিক্রয় অনুমোদন জারি করে উক্ত প্রট আমার নিকট থেকে সাব-কবলা করে নিয়ে বাকি টাকা পরিশোধ করিলে আমি আপনাদের অবশিষ্ট ৫ কোটি টাকা পরিশোধ করিতে পারিব ।”(Annexure-E) the petitioner made a representation to the respondent bank on 21-12-2016, prior to expiry of the stipulated period, and made a prayer to adjust Taka 900 lac against his respective loan accounts and to allow him further 6(six) months to pay the balance Taka 500 lac against Taka 1400 lac, but without interest Considering the context, the prayer of the petitioner was allowed by the Board of Directors of the respondent bank in its 1078th meeting dated 29-12-2016(Annexure-F) upon extending the period of payment up to 30- 6-2017 from 29-12-2016 with direction upon the petitioner to pay interest at 13% pa on the remaining settlement amount. In default, settlement arrangement would be cancelled and the petitioner would be liable to pay the entire outstanding dues with interest, again the petitioner failed to pay within time for not being able to obtain permission from the Ministry concern to sell the property situated at Tejgaon Industrial Area. To that effect by filing application on 27-6-2017(Annexure-C) he again sought 3(three) months’ time. The respondent bank did not allow his prayer, rather consequent to its letter dated 8-1-2017(Annexure-F) had cancelled the settlement arrangement vide letter dated 12-7-2017(Annexure-VIII lo the affidavit-in-opposition) with direction upon the petitioner to adjust the entire liability with upto date interest. 

 18. From the above chronology of facts it is apparent that the petitioner was always vigilant in paying off the defaulted loan amount and to that effect he made a prayer to the respondent bank on 1-9-2016, when Artha Rin Suit was pending, to pay off the amount as stated therein at one go subject to waiver of interest/penalty etc. The respondent bank also responded thereto and allowed him time towards settlement of the amount by 29-12-2016 with payment of Taka 1400 lac. The petitioner managed to pay Taka 900 lac but to pay the remaining Taka 500 lac within time, which he subsequently paid on 26-11-2017 and 28-11-2017 respectively but after the expiry of the time so was extended subsequently by the Board of Directors of the respondent bank i.e., more than 5(five) months after the extended period. 

 19. In this regard, we cannot overlook the accommodation the respondent bank gave to the petitioner on every occasion he asked for and he also gave effort to comply therewith. However, if we look at the reason behind the delay in paying off the balance Taka 500 lac by the petitioner then it could be seen that said delay was not intentional. The petitioner in every of his representations so made before the respondent bank had categorically stated that the required money was being arranged by selling off his industrial plot situated at Tejgaon Industrial Area for which he required approval from the concerned Ministry, which he could not obtain within the time so fixed by the respondent bank. Ultimately, on obtaining clearance he sold off the said property and accordingly, paid off the balance amount of Taka 500 lac, but meanwhile more than 5(five) months had elapsed after the date so fixed by the bank on 29-12-2016. 

 21. It is fact that in the 1078th meeting dated 29-12-2016 (Annexure-F) when the Board of Directors of the respondent bank extended time for another 6(six) months a default clause was inserted in its letter dated 8-1-2017 that if the petitioner failed to pay within time he would be liable to pay the entire outstanding dues with interest. The petitioner having failed to comply, the settlement arrangement was cancelled by the respondent bank on 12-7-2017 (Annexure-VIII) and ultimately, it fixed Taka 200 lac being classified (BL) liability in its meeting dated 1-8-2018 (Annexure-L). Considering the context of the case, the discretionary power so has been exercised by the Board of Directors of the respondent bank in fixing the said liability cannot be said as just and fair.
